entry.title: This Robot Is Unlike Any Other On The Market

media:group.media:title: This Robot Is Unlike Any Other On The Market
media:group.media:description:
This week I discovered the Flourish 1, a $3,500 robot that uses a Raspberry Pi instead of expensive hardware and can learn household chores just by watching you move your phone.
It focuses on practical tasks instead of flashy features, and the price reflects that.
Only 50 are being made in the first batch with shipping planned for December.
Would you rather get this instead of an ultra advanced $20,000 robot?
#Robotics #FutureTech #AI #AInews

media:group.media:description:

I let it run my Megabonk game test for almost 20 HOURS… and the result is kind of insane.
It's also surprisingly affordable. Opus 5.5 is available on Claude’s Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, so you can access it starting with the $20/month Pro plan.

That price-to-performance ratio is pretty wild for a model this good at long-running coding tasks.
Have you tried Opus 5.5 yet?

entry.title: This AI Model Is INSANELY Fast & Cheap

media:group.media:title: This AI Model Is INSANELY Fast & Cheap
media:group.media:description:
This AI model doesn’t use… WORDS?
It’s called Jev, from Typesafe AI, and instead of generating paragraphs or code text, it skips straight to making a decision.
Instead of text, it’s outputs are things like:→ a choice→ a score→ true/false
That makes it insanely fast and ridiculously cheap. Input costs start at just 4¢ per million tokens, and outputs are free because they’re apparently too cheap to meter.
Would you actually build with something like this?
#ai #ainews #futuretech #aimodel

entry.title: This Robot Looks DEMONIC... On Purpose?

media:group.media:title: This Robot Looks DEMONIC... On Purpose?
media:group.media:description:
This robot looks straight up like a fantasy movie villain, but it was designed like that on purpose.
Despite how it looks, the Threehalves robot's design actually makes perfect sense: four legs for stability, tools that attach directly to its wrists, and horns that house cameras for a remote operator.
The goal is to let skilled workers tackle dangerous jobs from a safe distance, like wildfire zones, collapsed buildings, and toxic environments.
It’s still a half-built proof of concept. But this is the kind of robotics idea I want to see work. Even if I’d absolutely run the other way if I saw it in the woods.
#Robotics #FutureTech #AInews #ai

entry.title: He Built The Ultimate Spy Tool (Free and Open-Source)

media:group.media:title: He Built The Ultimate Spy Tool (Free and Open-Source)
media:group.media:description:
Check out God's Eye View: https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view https://www.spatialintelligence.ai/
What if you could turn your computer into a spy movie command center using real-world data? I sat down with Bilawal Sidhu to explore God's Eye View, his open-source tool that brings flights, satellites, ships, traffic, and more into one interactive 3D globe.
We dive into how he built it with AI, try out its voice controls, and explore everything from military flight data to public traffic cameras and NASA fire detections. Bilawal also shows how people are using it to reconstruct real-world events, and I walk through getting it running on your own computer.
The project is open source, and many of the data sources are free for personal use. Some features require API keys, and voice interaction or heavier usage can add costs.
